one_liner: Rust pointwise Japanese word segmenter that runs KyTea's own models about 7.6-8.7x faster than KyTea (C++).
what_it_does: Vaporetto splits Japanese text into words by scoring every character boundary with a linear classifier (KyTea's pointwise method), and can optionally predict part-of-speech and reading tags. The Rust API is Model::read, Predictor::new(model, predict_tags), then predictor.predict(&mut sentence) on a reusable Sentence; workspace CLIs convert KyTea models, train new ones, run prediction and edit model weights, and there are a Python wrapper, a tantivy tokenizer crate and a Wasm demo. It is not a drop-in for KyTea's C++ API or command line, but a converted KyTea model gives KyTea's segmentation.
how_it_is_fast: All character n-gram features and dictionary words go into one double-array Aho-Corasick automaton (daachorse, charwise variant by default), and each pattern's weight vector is pre-merged with the weights of its suffix patterns at model-build time, so one overlapping scan of the sentence adds one precomputed weight vector per match to the boundary-score array instead of looking up every n-gram around every boundary. Character-type features are scored from a cache (cache-type-score), and weights are 32-bit integers in fixed 8-lane arrays (fix-weight-length) so the additions vectorize without intrinsics. The gain is algorithmic restructuring of the same model, not Rust versus C++.
when_to_use: High-throughput Japanese word segmentation (search indexing, corpus preprocessing for ML) where boundary decisions are enough and full morphological analysis is not needed
Existing KyTea users who want the same model's segmentation faster: convert the .mod file with convert_kytea_model and keep the behaviour
Full-text search on tantivy (vaporetto_tantivy crate) or Python pipelines (python-vaporetto)
Browser or embedded targets: the crate builds with no_std plus alloc and has a Wasm demo
Fixing specific mis-segmentations without retraining, by editing per-pattern boundary weights with manipulate_model
when_not_to_use: Full morphological analysis (lemmas, conjugation forms, UniDic fields): tag prediction is labelled experimental and lemma/UniDic-ID models are an open request (#148); a MeCab-style analyser such as Vibrato fits better
Short-lived processes where startup dominates: the published timings exclude model loading, and the README says the default charwise automaton can make model loading slower
Loading predictors from untrusted bytes: Predictor::deserialize_from_slice_unchecked is an unsafe fn that skips validation (Model::read validates)
Pipelines that need a stable model file format: bincode is unmaintained and the maintainer has chosen postcard as its replacement (issue #153, PR #156), so serialized files may change
Non-Japanese KyTea models on older releases: Chinese KyTea models failed to convert ('unsupported character type: 4', issue #110) until PR #111 in September 2023

integration.dependencies: bincode 2, daachorse 1, hashbrown 0.15; liblinear only with the train feature; distribution models are zstd-compressed and must be decompressed outside the API (zstd or ruzstd crate)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.85 for the released 0.6.5 (main branch now declares 1.88); the optional portable-simd feature needs nightly
integration.platforms: any target with alloc (no_std supported, Wasm demo); no architecture-specific intrinsics
integration.thread_safety: predict takes &self plus a caller-owned &mut Sentence, so one Predictor can serve many threads with one Sentence each; Send/Sync guarantees are not documented
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — reads converted KyTea models and reproduces KyTea word segmentation, but exposes a different Rust API and CLI, and the README documents KyTea model conversion for word segmentation only

gotchas: The README's 8.7x is the charwise-automaton build (25.3 ms vs KyTea 219.6 ms), which is now the default feature; the default build at the time measured 29.0 ms (7.6x), and the authors' own papers report 5.7x (arXiv 2406.17185) and 5.4x (NLP2022), so expect roughly 5-9x depending on version and machine.

The benchmark code exists outside the repo: legalforce-research/tokenizer-speed-bench (commits by the Vaporetto author; run_all.sh 100 iterations on wagahaiwa_nekodearu.txt with KyTea model jp-0.4.7-5). Both bench/kytea-bench/main.cc and bench/vaporetto-bench load the model before the timer, read all lines into memory first and time only segmentation, KyTea's library is built by its own configure at -O3 (bench main -O2 at the March 2022 commit 84383b2) and Vaporetto with cargo --release, so no harness flaw was found. Caveats: neither side's word count is checked against the other, and the charwise row is not in the harness at that commit (it pins Vaporetto rev a8308cd without the charwise feature). The harness plus the wiki's compiler versions and CPU could support a move from tier C to B or A.
Sentence::update_raw returns an error for empty text, and the benchmark harness unwraps it, so strip empty lines before tokenizing.
Weights are 32-bit integers; the README warns that hand-edited dictionary weights can overflow the boundary total.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: None of the listed siblings segments Japanese: the Rust regex crate and the LangArena word-count rows split on whitespace or patterns. Within the catalog, use Vibrato (also daac-tools) when you need MeCab-dictionary morphological analysis, and Vaporetto when word boundaries (optionally with tags) from a KyTea-style model are enough and speed matters most.
verified_claims_summary: The first-party wiki (Vaporetto v0.4.0, Rust 1.60.0 and GCC 11.2.0 on an Intel Core i7-8086K under CentOS 7.5) tokenized Natsume Soseki's 'I Am a Cat' 100 times with the same KyTea compact SVM model: KyTea (2020-04-03) 219.6 ms vs Vaporetto 29.0 ms (7.6x) and the charwise build 25.3 ms (8.7x), ratios derived from page data. The matching public harness (tokenizer-speed-bench) excludes model loading on both sides and times only segmentation; MeCab, Lindera, sudachi.rs and rust-tinysegmenter rows use other dictionaries or algorithms and are not like-for-like.
status_note: Maintained at a slow pace (last commit 2026-07-20, last crate release 0.6.5 on 2025-03-17, 331k downloads with 74.6k recent, a serialization switch to postcard in progress); MIT or Apache-2.0 and copyable, with free distributed models and KyTea model conversion.
